name: Hashcat - Rule Function Reference
description: Rules mutate each wordlist candidate on the fly (capitalize, leetspeak, append digits/symbols) so one base list covers many realistic variants. Bundled rules live in /usr/share/hashcat/rules; you can also write your own, one function per transformation.

examples.label: Dictionary attack with a bundled rule
OSCP Ch15 — preview mutations without cracking (pipe through --stdout to inspect candidates)

notes: Chain functions on one line (e.g. `c so0 $!` = capitalize, o->0, append !). best64.rule and rockyou-30000.rule are good defaults. Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 15 (Password Attacks).

recommended.note: Use a rule to expand a wordlist to a file.

variations.label: Common rule functions
variations.command:
:      - Do nothing (pass through)
l      - Lowercase all letters
u      - Uppercase all letters
c      - Capitalize first, lowercase rest
sXY    - Replace all X with Y (e.g. so0)
$X     - Append character X (e.g. $!)
^X     - Prepend character X
r      - Reverse the word
d      - Duplicate the word

variations.label: Example custom rule file
variations.command:
cat custom.rule
:
c
so0
c so0
sa@
c sa@
$!
$! c
$! so0
$! c so0 sa@
